subject: Post-call: Quantica model fit + quantization tradeoffs and next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Emily Tran <emily@quanticahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + suggested eval plan for Quantica

Thanks Emily — great conversation earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we have alignment.

Call highlights:
- Primary objective: improve triage accuracy for radiology reports while keeping 95th percentile latency under 150ms for API calls.
- Risk tolerance: extremely low on clinical hallucinations; any increase in false positives must be surfaced.
- Current infra note: Quantica will start with a dedicated pool (us-west) and may evaluate a private deployment later.

Recommended immediate plan (what we’ll run in the next 7–10 days):
1) Benchmark baseline models on your prompt set (attached): ||recommended candidates||
   - small/high-throughput: Mistral-7B (FP16 / AWQ) — fastest per-token, good on short prompts
   - medium/balanced: Llama-2-13B (GPTQ 4-bit) — better clinical reasoning, moderate throughput
   - high-quality: Falcon-40B-instruct (FP8 evaluation) — best accuracy on long context tests but higher cost

2) Quantization/throughput trade study (we’ll run these variants in parallel):
   - AWQ (activation-aware weight quant) vs GPTQ 4-bit (post-training) vs FP8 mixed precision
   - Measure: accuracy on labeled prompt set, hallucination rate (manual sample), token latency p50/p95, GPU util, and end-to-end cost per 1k requests.

3) Quality regression guardrails:
   - Use our evaluation harness to compute Delta-BLEU and a custom clinical-fidelity score on the benchmark.
   - If hallucination increases >1.5x or clinical-fidelity drops >3 points, we fail the variant and fallback to a safer model.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Jordan: upload prompt set and call recording to the HubSpot deal (done) — ETA: now (attachments included).
- Rishi: propose a short quant-eval plan with exact metrics and scripts — ETA: tomorrow EOD.
- Emily: confirm SLA targets and any additional PII/redaction constraints — ETA: Monday 4/26.

Attachments: prompt-pack-v1.txt (prompt templates + golden labels), quant-eval-plan.csv (blank template), call_recording-20270422.mp3
Benchmarks: https://redwood-benchmarks.internal/2027/med-nlp-latency-compare

I’ll schedule a 30-minute follow-up on April 27 to review initial run results — let me know if that works for your team.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

From: Emily Tran <emily@quanticahealth.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Clinical AI Team <clinical-ai@quanticahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + suggested eval plan for Quantica

Thanks Jordan — this is helpful. Quick notes from our side:

- Latency target: p95 <= 150ms is firm for triage flows; background batch jobs can be slower.
- Data sensitivity: PHI present in some examples; we require KMS-backed encryption and audit logs for the private deployment evaluation.
- Quality: clinical-team wants to prioritize reducing hallucinations over raw throughput — acceptable to take a small cost increase if hallucination rate drops.

Questions:
1) Can you prioritize variants that bias toward safety (e.g., Llama-2-13B GPTQ before AWQ)?
2) Do you have an automated hallucination checker or should we do manual spot checks?

We can confirm SLA and security asks Monday. Also please loop in your quant expert if possible — we want to understand the expected deltas between AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 for medical text.

Emily
Emily Tran
Clinical ML Lead | Quantica Health
emily@quanticahealth.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Emily Tran <emily@quanticahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + suggested eval plan for Quantica

Great questions — thanks. Short answers:
- We’ll prioritize the safer-leaning variants first (Llama-2-13B GPTQ) as you requested. If that meets accuracy constraints, we’ll test AWQ variants to see if latency gains are possible without regression.
- Redwood provides a hallucination scoring harness that compares generated outputs to golden labels and flags divergence types (fabrication, omission, hallucinated entities). We’ll run automated checks and pair them with manual spot checks from your clinical reviewers.

Rishi — I’ve looped you in to own the quant evaluation matrix and scripts. Can you outline the metrics you’ll collect and a short cutoff policy for automatic failures?

Emily — would Tuesday 4/27 09:30 PT work for the 30-min review?

Jordan

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Emily Tran <emily@quanticahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quant plan: AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8 — short summary + attached eval plan

Hi all — quick technical primer and proposed pass/fail rules (see attached quant-eval-plan.csv for script hooks). I kept this short for the clinical team.

Summary of quant variants (high level):
- AWQ (activation-aware weights): tends to preserve activations distribution for decoder heads; best latency wins on 7–13B models; occasional small shifts on named-entity recall for clinical entities.
- GPTQ (per-channel 4-bit): generally stable for instruction tasks; can introduce subtle wording changes but often keeps core facts intact. Good midpoint for Llama-2-13B.
- FP8 (mixed precision): closest to FP16 in quality, lower throughput improvement vs 4-bit options but safest on hallucination risk for larger models (40B+).

Metrics we’ll collect automatically (scripts in CSV):
- Accuracy (micro F1) on labeled set
- Clinical-fidelity score (custom: weighted precision on diagnoses/medications)
- Hallucination rate (auto flags + manual sample rate)
- Latency p50/p95/end-to-end (including our prefix caching overhead)
- Throughput (tokens/sec) and estimated cost per 1k requests

Pass/fail (short):
- Fail if hallucination rate increases >1.5x OR clinical-fidelity drops >3 points relative to FP16 baseline.
- Secondary flag if p95 > 150ms for API path. Those variants can be considered only for async/batch routes.

Practical next steps I’ll run (timeline):
- Today: kick off baseline FP16 runs on your prompt-pack (sanitized subset) — outputs + metrics to shared bucket.
- Tomorrow: run Llama-2-13B GPTQ and AWQ variants; FP8 check on Falcon-40B if you want that included (you indicated higher-cost ok for quality).
- Monday: collate results + create short decision matrix for the April 27 call.

Note on hallucination checking: automated checks catch entity hallucinations well but clinical nuance (wrong side, wrong dosage) still needs manual review. Plan to sample 200 outputs for manual review per variant.

Attachments: quant-eval-plan.csv (script list + metric hooks)

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
